title: Noncopyable Generics
hints: `~Copyable` in a generic constraint removes the implicit `Copyable` requirement.
A vault containing a noncopyable item must itself be `~Copyable`; store with a `consuming` parameter.
Extract with `item.take()`, which moves the value out and leaves `nil`.
jsBridge: Generics that accept `~Copyable` types can hold unique resources in containers without copying. There's no JS parallel. It's Rust-style ownership reaching generic code.

compass.q: No JS equivalent exists. What problem (unique ownership of resources) is this solving?
Why must a generic opt in with `~Copyable`? What would break if all generics accepted noncopyable types?
`Optional<T: ~Copyable>`: how does the standard library support noncopyable optionals?
Library authors, not app authors, benefit most. Agree or disagree?
